lesson: Two verified findings. (1) BLOCKING, performance P1, and it matches the orchestrator's own repeated measurement: LLM_SELECTOR_MAX_TOKENS 2048 does not reach the sub-5-second goal. Measured with one prior turn: 2048 -> 5370ms, 4610ms, 19299ms (1153, 1170, 2048 output tokens); 512 -> 5610ms, 2667ms, 5833ms (512 every time). The cap NEVER truncates - every run at 256, 512 and 2048 returned stopReason tool_use with a valid tool block, because the model emits the tool call and THEN keeps writing, so output saturates at the cap and lower is strictly better. Set LLM_SELECTOR_MAX_TOKENS to 512. Keep the retry cap HIGHER than the first so attempt two still differs (2048 is fine); do not go to 256, where one sample returned unsupported for a harder question at 114 tokens - below the cap, so not truncation, but not worth the risk on one sample. The contract's C1 names 2048 and its 'headroom' justification is inverted by this evidence; this change is made under the blocking review finding and must be recorded as superseding that value. Update any test that asserts the specific number. (2) P2, bedrock.provider.ts:400: when the first call returns no_tool_block and the retry succeeds, 'return second' DISCARDS first.usage. chat.service.ts:182 feeds sel.usage into the audit event, so a retried question under-reports its real token spend in audit_events. Sum inputTokens, outputTokens and totalTokens across BOTH attempts before returning, and cover it with a leaf.
